_meta.description: HR task templates for AI-Prowler HR module. Every row becomes a task with instructions, form links, and escalation rules.

due_anchor_legend.start_date: Days relative to employee start date (negative = before start)
due_anchor_legend.hire_date: Days from offer acceptance / hire date

base.name: Generate and send offer letter
base.instructions: Generate offer letter from template. Must include: legal name, job title, annual salary, start date, employment type (full-time/part-time/contract), at-will statement, and reporting manager. Email or deliver to candidate. Mark as sent in app.
base.penalty: No legal penalty, but no binding offer without written confirmation.

base.name: Provide FCRA disclosure to candidate
base.instructions: Federal law (FCRA) requires you to provide a clear and conspicuous written disclosure to the candidate — separate from any other document — before running a background check. Provide this notice and obtain signed authorization. Use the CFPB model notice.
base.penalty: $1,000+ per willful violation. Class action exposure.

base.name: Complete background check
base.instructions: Initiate background check through your vendor. FCRA adverse action: if result is adverse and you plan to deny, you MUST provide: (1) pre-adverse action notice + copy of report + Summary of Rights, (2) wait reasonable time, (3) then adverse action notice.
base.penalty: FCRA adverse action violations: $1,000+ per incident.

base.name: Upload signed offer letter
base.instructions: After candidate signs the offer letter, upload a scan of the fully executed offer letter to this employee's /hiring/ folder.
base.penalty: Without executed offer letter: compensation disputes have no written baseline.

base.name: Report new hire to state directory
base.instructions: ALL employers must report every new hire to the state new hire directory within 20 days. Report by submitting employee name, address, SSN, hire date, and company EIN. Required by federal law (PRWORA) — no size exemption. State portal is auto-linked based on the employee's work state.
base.penalty: Up to $25/employee. $500 if conspiracy with employee.

base.name: Complete payroll system setup for this employee
base.instructions: Add this employee to your payroll platform before the first paycheck runs. Required data: legal name, SSN, address, work state, W-4 withholding data, state tax form data, pay type, pay rate, pay frequency, direct deposit bank info, benefits deductions.
base.penalty: Employee cannot be paid without payroll system setup.

base.name: Provision work email and accounts
base.instructions: Create {first.last}@company.com. Set up: SSO/identity provider, Slack, email client, required SaaS tools. Document each system provisioned. Confirm with manager which tools are needed for this role.
base.penalty: Work email required before employee can complete self-service portal login on Day 1.

base.name: Order or stage equipment
base.instructions: Remote employee: ship to home address shown in employee record. On-site: stage at assigned desk. Include: laptop (configured with company image), charger, peripherals. Track asset serial numbers in task notes.
base.penalty: Employee cannot work without equipment on Day 1.

base.name: Create and share orientation schedule
base.instructions: Build the Day 1 orientation schedule: manager welcome (30-60 min), HR orientation (benefits, policies, culture), I-9 document review session, IT setup session. Share with manager and new employee. Block calendars. I-9 must be completed within 3 business days — schedule dedicated time.
base.penalty: Without I-9 session scheduled, Day 3 deadline may be missed.

base.name: Assign buddy or mentor
base.instructions: Select a buddy from the team for this employee's first 30 days. Notify the buddy of the start date, the new employee's name, role, and first-week schedule. Buddy should reach out by personal email before Day 1.
base.penalty: Buddy programs significantly improve 90-day retention rates.

base.name: Confirm workplace posters ready
base.instructions: ON-SITE: Confirm 6 federal posters displayed in a common area: (1) OSHA Job Safety and Health, (2) EEOC Know Your Rights, (3) FLSA Minimum Wage, (4) FMLA Employee Rights (50+ employees), (5) EPPA, (6) USERRA. Also post applicable state posters. REMOTE: Prepare digital poster pack email to send Day 1. All posters are FREE at dol.gov/general/topics/posters.
base.penalty: OSHA citation and penalty for failure to post. Separate state penalties.

base.name: I-9 Section 1 — Employee completes
base.instructions: You must complete the top portion of Form I-9 on or before your first day of work. Attest to your work authorization status. You'll need to show original identity documents (not copies) to your HR contact. Bring a passport, OR a driver's license AND Social Security card.
base.penalty: Company cannot allow employee to work without completed I-9 Section 1.

base.name: I-9 Section 2 — HR verifies documents
base.instructions: Physically examine the employee's original identity and work authorization documents in person (or via authorized representative for remote employees). Accept List A OR List B+C. Record document title, issuing authority, number, and expiration date. Sign and date Section 2. Upload scan to /onboarding/ folder. Set expiration date if work authorization has an end date.
base.penalty: $272–$2,726 per form violation (paperwork). $698–$27,894 per knowingly unauthorized worker.

base.name: Federal W-4 — Employee completes
base.instructions: This form tells your employer how much federal income tax to take out of your paycheck. Complete based on your filing status. Download, complete, sign, and upload a scan. You can update it at any time.
base.penalty: Without W-4: employer must withhold at maximum (Single, 0 allowances) rate.

base.name: State tax withholding form — Employee completes
base.instructions: Your state requires a state income tax withholding form in addition to the federal W-4. Download the form for your state (shown below), complete, sign, and upload a scan.
base.penalty: Without state form: state applies default withholding rate.

base.name: Direct deposit authorization
base.instructions: Provide your bank's routing number and checking account number. The easiest way is to attach a voided check or bank letter. This is how your paycheck will be deposited. Upload the voided check or completed authorization form.
base.penalty: Without direct deposit setup: payroll cannot process your paycheck electronically. May delay first paycheck.

base.name: Employee handbook acknowledgment
base.instructions: Read the employee handbook. Then sign the acknowledgment page confirming you have received it and agree to follow the company's policies. Upload a scan of the signed acknowledgment.
base.penalty: Without signed acknowledgment, policy enforcement is harder in disputes.

base.name: Emergency contact form
base.instructions: Provide the name, phone number, and relationship of one or two emergency contacts. This information is used only in the event of a workplace emergency. You can update it at any time in My Profile.
base.penalty: Company policy.

base.name: HIPAA Privacy Notice acknowledgment
base.instructions: If the company offers a group health plan, federal law requires you to receive and acknowledge the HIPAA Notice of Privacy Practices. Read it and upload the signed acknowledgment.
base.penalty: Federal HIPAA requirement. HHS OCR civil monetary penalties apply.

base.name: IT setup session
base.instructions: Complete laptop configuration, email setup, VPN access, and all required software. IT documents each system accessed and has employee sign the IT asset receipt and acceptable use policy.
base.penalty: Access must be documented for security audit trail.

base.name: Manager welcome meeting
base.instructions: 30-60 minute one-on-one. Cover: role expectations and first priorities, team structure and who to go to for what, the 30-day goals framework, a walkthrough of the employee's onboarding task list. This meeting is the top predictor of 90-day retention.
base.penalty: Research shows Day 1 manager meeting is the top predictor of 90-day retention.

base.name: Send digital poster pack to remote employee
base.instructions: Email the following free federal poster PDFs to the employee's work email: (1) OSHA osha.gov/publications/poster, (2) EEOC eeoc.gov/poster, (3) FLSA dol.gov, (4) FMLA dol.gov, (5) EPPA dol.gov, (6) USERRA dol.gov. Also include applicable state labor law poster links.
base.penalty: DOL recommends digital delivery for remote workers as substitute for physical posting.

base.name: Document FLSA classification
base.instructions: Record whether this employee is Exempt or Non-Exempt under the Fair Labor Standards Act. Exempt requires BOTH: salary of $684+/week ($35,568/year) AND passing the duties test (executive, administrative, professional, computer, or outside sales). If either test fails, employee is non-exempt and entitled to overtime. Document the basis in the notes field.
base.penalty: Misclassification is one of the most common and costly wage/hour violations. Back wages + liquidated damages + attorney fees.

base.name: Verify state minimum wage compliance
base.instructions: Verify this employee's hourly rate (or equivalent) meets the state minimum wage for their work state. The app flags this automatically if the rate is below the threshold. Review and correct immediately if flagged.
base.penalty: Back pay liability for all hours worked below minimum wage + civil penalties.

base.name: Assign compliance and safety training
base.instructions: Assign all required training: (1) Harassment prevention (legally required in CA, NY, IL, CT, ME, WA), (2) Data security and acceptable use, (3) Workplace safety/OSHA orientation, (4) Industry-specific compliance if applicable. Track completion in task notes.
base.penalty: CA SB 1343: harassment training required for all employees within 6 months of hire.

CA.instructions: CA SB 1343 requires 1 hour of harassment prevention training for non-supervisory employees within 6 months of hire. Supervisors require 2 hours.

base.name: Team introduction meetings
base.instructions: Schedule and complete brief intro meetings between the new employee and all direct team members and key cross-functional partners. 15-30 minutes each. A group lunch or team session is an efficient alternative.
base.penalty: Integration with team by end of Week 1 strongly predicts 30-day retention.

base.name: Grant role-specific system access
base.instructions: Grant access to all systems required for this role. Manager provides the access list. IT implements. Employee signs an access acknowledgment. Document each system granted in task notes. Do NOT grant access to systems not required for the role (least privilege).
base.penalty: Document access for security audit. Over-provisioning increases breach risk.

base.name: Draft 30-day goals
base.instructions: Manager and employee collaborate to draft first 30-day goals — typically 3-5 specific, measurable objectives. Document goals in task notes or upload a written goals document. These will be reviewed at the 30-day check-in.
base.penalty: Employees with clear 30-day goals are significantly more likely to remain at 90 days.

base.name: Benefits enrollment deadline
base.instructions: HARD DEADLINE: You have 30 days from your start date to enroll in company benefits: health, dental, vision, 401(k). After this window closes, you must wait until the next open enrollment unless you have a qualifying life event (marriage, birth, loss of other coverage). Contact HR immediately with questions.
base.penalty: Missing benefits window means employee may go uninsured for up to a year.

base.name: 30-day review meeting
base.instructions: Hold a dedicated 30-minute check-in. Review 30-day goals: what was accomplished, what needs adjustment. Ask: Is the role what you expected? Do you have what you need? Any concerns? Document outcome in task notes.
base.penalty: The 30-day conversation is a leading indicator of 90-day retention.

base.name: COBRA General Notice (if health plan)
base.instructions: If the company offers a group health plan, federal law requires providing the COBRA General Notice to all new participants within 90 days of plan enrollment. The plan administrator can provide this — upload confirmation to /onboarding/.
base.penalty: $110/day penalty for failure to provide required COBRA notices.

base.name: WA Cares Fund disclosure
base.instructions: Inform Washington employees about the WA Cares Fund — a mandatory long-term care insurance program funded by a 0.58% employee payroll deduction. Provide the opt-out form if the employee has qualifying private long-term care insurance. Upload acknowledgment to /onboarding/.
base.penalty: Required for all WA employees. Deduction begins with first paycheck.

base.name: 90-day performance check-in
base.instructions: 60-90 minute formal review. Review all goals set over the first 90 days. Assess performance against expectations. Document: overall assessment (Meets/Below/Exceeds), specific strengths and development areas, 6-month goals, any concerns. This meeting ends the probationary period.
base.penalty: Probationary period end without formal review creates documentation risk.

base.name: Confirm probationary period end
base.instructions: Based on the 90-day check-in, confirm the employee's continued employment. Update the employee record: probationary period ended (date). If extending probation or taking action, document the reason and consult legal if needed.
base.penalty: Undocumented probation extensions can complicate subsequent employment actions.

offboarding.name: Record termination event
offboarding.instructions: Enter: termination type (voluntary/involuntary/layoff/retirement), effective date, last day of work, and reason code. This triggers all downstream offboarding tasks automatically.
offboarding.penalty: Failure to record triggers no downstream tasks — all compliance deadlines missed.

offboarding.name: Notify IT — revoke system access
offboarding.instructions: IMMEDIATELY revoke: email, SSO, VPN, all SaaS tools, building access. Document the exact time of revocation for each system. IT must confirm completion in task notes.
offboarding.penalty: Failure to revoke access is a security incident. May violate contractual obligations.

offboarding.name: Calculate and issue final paycheck
offboarding.instructions: Calculate final paycheck including all accrued but unused PTO (if required by state). Issue within the state-specific deadline shown below. Final pay deadline varies by state and termination type.

penalty_by_state.CA: CA involuntary: SAME DAY. CA voluntary: 72 hours. Waiting time penalty = 1 day's wages per day late, up to 30 days.
penalty_by_state.TX: TX involuntary: within 6 days. TX voluntary: next regular payday.
penalty_by_state.WA: WA: end of current pay period.
penalty_by_state.MA: MA: next payday or the following Saturday, whichever comes first.

offboarding.name: Send COBRA qualifying event notice to plan admin
offboarding.instructions: Notify your group health plan administrator of the qualifying event within 30 days of termination. The plan admin must then send the election notice to the employee within 14 days. Upload confirmation of notification to /termination/ folder.

offboarding.name: Equipment return checklist
offboarding.instructions: Track return of: laptop, badge/key card, keys, company credit card, parking pass. Mark each item returned in task notes. IT must verify data has been wiped from returned devices.
offboarding.penalty: Unreturned equipment creates asset loss and potential data security issue.

offboarding.name: Non-compete validity check
offboarding.instructions: Check the employee's work state before presenting a separation agreement with a non-compete clause. CA, MN, ND, and OK: non-compete clauses are void by state law. Do NOT enforce or threaten enforcement in these states. Remove from separation agreement.
offboarding.penalty: Enforcing void non-competes in CA/MN/ND/OK can expose company to litigation from the employee.

offboarding.name: Exit interview
offboarding.instructions: Conduct an exit interview on or within 3 days of last day. Upload completed exit interview form to /termination/ folder. This is optional but provides valuable retention intelligence.
offboarding.penalty: Optional but valuable for understanding turnover patterns.

annual.name: Annual minimum wage check
annual.instructions: State minimum wages typically increase January 1. The app checks each active employee's hourly equivalent against the current minimum wage for their work state. Review and update pay rates immediately for any employee below the new minimum.
annual.penalty: Paying below minimum wage is an FLSA violation. Back wages + liquidated damages.

annual.name: Confirm annual federal poster updates
annual.instructions: Federal workplace posters are updated when laws change. Confirm all posted versions are current at dol.gov/general/topics/posters. Download and replace any outdated posters. For remote employees, resend the updated digital poster pack.
annual.penalty: Outdated posters may trigger compliance violations when laws change.
